titulo: Stuck in 2026, Ep. 2: Power in a Pocket
tema: Stuck in 2026, episode 2: Kip learns how a lithium-ion power bank stores and releases energy, and finds out he must build a time machine
perguntaCentral: Where does a power bank keep its energy, and how does it get out?

reliquia.descricao: an ordinary pocket-sized power bank from the 2020s: a dark grey rounded rectangle with four small charge lights in a row and one charging port, connected with a plain white charging cable

cenas.acao: In Ben's garage, Kip taps his cracked, dark Chrono-Band again and again and nothing happens.
cenas.narracao: Stuck in 2026, my *Chrono-Band* was dead. I tapped it again and again. Nothing. Without power, I had no way home.
cenas.visual: Ben's garage: workbench with Ben's watch ticking on it, pegboard, roll-up door. Kip taps his cracked dark band at 'tapped' and again at 'again'; at 'Nothing' a grey cross over the band; at 'way home' a faded portal thought-bubble pops and vanishes.

cenas.acao: Ben walks in, pulls a power bank from his pocket and holds it up.
cenas.narracao: Then Ben pulled a small brick from his pocket: a *power bank*, a lithium-ion battery that people carried around.
cenas.visual: Ben enters from the right, reaches into his shorts pocket at 'pulled', holds up a dark grey power bank with four lights at 'brick'; a label 'power bank' at 'power bank' and a small battery icon at 'lithium-ion'. Kip leans in, curious.

cenas.acao: Ben plugs a cable from the power bank into a tiny port on Kip's band; the lights blink and power flows.
cenas.narracao: His cable fit a tiny port on my band. The little lights blinked, and *power* started flowing in.
cenas.visual: Kip holds the power bank in his right hand; a white cable runs to the Chrono-Band on his left wrist, plugged at 'port'. At 'blinked' the four lights blink in sequence; at 'power' yellow dots flow along the cable and the cracked band glows faintly.

cenas.acao: Cutaway of a battery cell: lithium ions drift from the graphite side to the other side through the separator.
cenas.narracao: Inside the battery, *lithium ions* drift from one side to the other, through a thin wall called a separator.
cenas.visual: Big cell cutaway: graphite layers on the left, metal-oxide side on the right, light-blue electrolyte between, a dashed separator wall in the middle. At 'lithium ions' small cyan '+' balls light up in the graphite; at 'drift' they float right, through the separator; at 'separator' the wall is labelled. Kip small in a corner.

cenas.acao: Electrons bounce off the separator and go the long way through an outside wire that lights Kip's band; then charging reverses the flow.
cenas.narracao: But the separator blocks *electrons*. So they take the long way, out through the wire, powering my band. Charging pushes everything back.
cenas.visual: Same cutaway. At 'blocks' yellow '−' dots bounce off the separator with a small cross; at 'long way' they leave the top of the graphite side, travel along an outside wire loop through a Chrono-Band icon that lights up at 'powering', and enter the other side. At 'Charging' a plug icon appears and every arrow flips: ions drift back left, electrons run back.

cenas.acao: Split screen: on Lumen, power waves flow through the air to everything; in 2026, a power bank charges at a wall socket, empties and charges again.
cenas.narracao: On Lumen, power flows through the air to everything. Here, people *store* it in batteries and charge them again and again.
cenas.visual: Bottom half (my time) first at 'Lumen': a tower sends cyan rings through the air to floating platforms and a citizen's device. Top half (old days) at 'Here': a power bank plugged into a wall socket; its four lights fill up at 'store', then empty and fill again at 'again and again'.

cenas.acao: The cracked band lights up for three seconds and projects a blueprint of a machine with six slots, two of them filled and four empty; then it goes dark.
cenas.narracao: Then my band lit up for *three seconds*. It showed a machine with four empty slots. To get home, I had to *build* one.
cenas.visual: Garage. At 'lit' the cracked band glows and projects a cyan hologram above Kip: a round machine outline with six slots. Two slots hold a crystal icon and a battery icon; four are dashed and empty, each with a '?' at 'four empty slots'. A 3-2-1 dot timer runs out and the hologram flickers off. Kip turns determined at 'build'; Ben smiles. 'TO BE CONTINUED' end card.
